leads.name: Bergulme (mountain elm) near the forestry office in Gosau
leads.reason: Not researched this pass: Gosau sits roughly 9km from Hallstatt centre, at the edge of or outside the day-trip cluster, and this pass kept to the four closest register candidates (three yews plus the nearby Bad Goisern one) per the max-four-candidates rule. Register text: 27m tall, one of the largest of its kind in Upper Austria, protected since 1980-12-18. Source: https://e-gov.ooe.gv.at/ndbinternet/NDBInternetGenisysDetail.jsp?mod=NSB&genisysInventarNr=nd147 and the Liste der Naturdenkmaeler im Bezirk Gmunden. Worth a look if a future pass covers Gosau, alongside the copper beech and school linden below (all three stand within about 100m of each other near the Gosau forestry office). [RESOLVED 2026-10-20, delivered as hst_007 flagged, in data/research/hallstatt-verified.json]

leads.name: Schul-Linde (school linden) in Gosau
leads.species: Large-leaved or Summer Lime (Tilia platyphyllos / Sommer-Linde)

location.note: Wikidata Q119889409, ~50m southwest of the Evangelical church in Gosau

leads.reason: Third Gosau candidate, ~800m from the other two; not pursued this pass. Register text (Liste der Naturdenkmaeler im Bezirk Gmunden): planted around 1790, girth 3.7m and height ~21m at designation. Stands next to a school -- per hard rule 10 school grounds need real evidence of genuinely open access before shipping (a public path, weekend opening, or a churchyard-like setting); this one is 50m from a church rather than clearly on school property, but that distinction should be checked properly rather than assumed, so it stays a lead.
